## Description

**What**: Update existing project documentation to reflect the new BRIDGE_USER_MAP repo variable, BRIDGE_ENV_ID requirement, the outbound checkpoint cursor behavior, and any sync-related troubleshooting that future agents will need.

**Why**: After this epic lands, the bridge subsystem behavior changes meaningfully — new repo variables, new precondition gates, new checkpoint file, new failure modes (BRIDGE_ALERT for migration, cold-start, etc.). Without documentation updates, future agents and operators will reason from stale information.

**Scope**:
- IN: CLAUDE.md (architecture section + quick reference if applicable), .claude/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md (sync-related troubleshooting entry), plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (new BRIDGE_USER_MAP and BRIDGE_ENV_ID entries with shape and defaults).
- OUT: creating new documentation files, updating user-facing docs that don't exist, scope-creep on bridge architecture rewrite.

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, CLAUDE.md's bridge architecture section mentions BRIDGE_USER_MAP, BRIDGE_ENV_ID, the outbound checkpoint cursor (.outbound-checkpoint.json), and the BRIDGE_ALERT migration semantics ← Satisfies: epic operational invariant — future agents have accurate sync subsystem awareness
- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md contains entries for BRIDGE_USER_MAP (JSON object, case-insensitive email keys → Jira accountId values) and BRIDGE_ENV_ID (non-empty UUID) ← Satisfies: same
- When this story is complete, .claude/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md has an entry covering the chronic silent-drop pattern (HEAD~1..HEAD blindness) with a pointer to the cursor-based recovery, plus the migration BRIDGE_ALERT semantics ← Satisfies: same

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Follow .claude/docs/DOCUMENTATION-GUIDE.md for formatting and structure.
- [Maintainability] Do NOT create new docs — only update existing files.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
